correctness.rationale: The proof shows directed cycles occur precisely from opposed complete theta paths; it exhaustively characterizes an edge reversal as illegal iff an alternative directed path exists. For non-direct edges, this forces a unique minority-sign edge on the original path plus a compatible fully oriented second path; for a possible direct edge its own additional obstruction is counted separately. The disjoint cases give the stated product and nonnegative interpretation. Its largest blocked-edge coefficient is 2 times the elementary-symmetric sum over all k−1 path lengths. Independent spanning-tree deletion classification proves that sum equals τ(G). The intrinsic zonotope dimension is \(n-1\). Direct independent topological-sort orientation enumeration and word/forest checks corroborate the result in 64 and 11 finite parameter cases; unrestricted validity follows from the symbolic proof, not those tests.

Spanning-tree/orientation tiling bijections enumerate chosen orientation representatives and have different equivalence relations; they do not imply a twice-spanning-tree count of minimum-degree orientations of all mixed-length theta graphs.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The new polynomial simultaneously distinguishes each possible number of nonreversible edges for arbitrary mixed path lengths and yields \(2\tau(G)\) simple vertices by extracting its extremal coefficient. Prior total counts, aggregate face counts, and tiling bijections have strictly less local information; no inspected theorem covers the exact claim.

value.rationale: Determines the complete local branching distribution of the acyclic-orientation flip graph for a natural infinite, multi-parameter graph family, not merely a preexisting global count. In particular the number of simple graphical-zonotope vertices collapses to precisely \(2\tau(G)\), a structural bridge between local polytope geometry and spanning-tree enumeration, despite arbitrary unequal path lengths and the direct-edge boundary. The full polynomial supplies exact distributions where f-vector or chromatic-polynomial data give only aggregates; the result is motivated by region wall counts and vertex simplicity rather than arbitrary small-case numerology.
